shared_elements: low-relief carved figure(s) in strict profile
standing/striding humanoid figure with one arm raised and bent at the elbow
elaborately curled, tightly rendered hair and beard rendered as rows of ringlets
long fringed/patterned robe reaching the ankles
held object in the raised hand (bucket/vessel and bowls)
feet in profile with detailed toes on a ground line
musculature/limbs rendered with schematic modelled contours
justification: Both show profile figures in long fringed robes with tightly curled ringleted hair and beards, one arm raised bent at the elbow while the other hand holds a vessel, carved in shallow relief with the same conventions for hair, drapery folds and feet — a fairly specific shared repertoire. The chief difference is content: A shows a single monumental bird-headed winged genius filling the field, while B shows a repeated procession of ordinary human attendants carrying bowls toward a figure at the right, so scale, subject and compositional scheme differ.
